text:
deploy-bot: Canary alert in eu-west-1 — embeddings pipeline p99 latency 2.1x baseline, token emission rate spike, and eval embedding drift >0.12. Auto-rollback candidate (threshold 2.0x). Flagging for human review @Elaine @Jordan :warning:

Elaine: seeing cosine similarity shift on the evaluation shard too. Not just latency — quality tanked for a subset of prompts.

Jordan: Confirmed — the canary included the new quantize-fast option for embedding model open-embed-v2.3.1. That flag reduces memory but may change output.

Priya: My recommendation: block auto-rollback for hosted traffic (we can fallback to open-embed-v2.2.9 automatic), but perform a manual targeted rollback for dedicated eu pools to avoid customer impact. We should pin the model for any affected Dedicated customers.

Carlos: Oncall taking lead for execution. I'll run the rollback once we have signoff. Which exact clusters to target? eu-dedicated-a and eu-dedicated-b?

Jordan: Yes — target eu-dedicated-a,b. Also add a temporary routing rule to shift 60% of canary traffic back to v2.2.9 while we validate.

Maya: I'll draft the customer blurb and release note update. Proposed copy: "We detected a regression in embeddings quality affecting a small subset of requests in eu-west-1. We are rolling back a recent optimization and will monitor closely. No data loss." Thoughts? :pencil2:

Elaine: good. Add a note that dedicated customers can request a freeze/pin if they rely on deterministic embeddings.

Priya: Operational steps (summarized):
1) Pin v2.2.9 for eu-dedicated clusters
2) Execute partial rollback on eu-dedicated pools
3) Route 60% canary -> v2.2.9 for 15m validation
4) If stable, scale rollback to 100% on dedicated pools and unpin if new patch validated
5) Publish customer note + release notes entry

Carlos: executing step 1 now.

```
# pin model for eu-dedicated pool
rictl model pin --cluster eu-dedicated-a,eu-dedicated-b --model open-embed-v2.2.9 --owner Carlos --reason "rollback from quantize-fast regression"
```

Carlos: pin command submitted, awaiting API ack... acked.

deploy-bot: Auto-rollback suppressed for eu-dedicated clusters by manual override (actor: Carlos) for 30m. Continuing to monitor metrics.

Maya: Customer note drafted and posted to #release-notes, ops-summaries. Sending to sales+CS in 10m for upstream customer outreach.

Jordan: After 15m validation window -> if p99 <= 1.2x baseline and embedding drift <0.04, we keep v2.2.9; otherwise escalate to expedited patch.

Elaine: I'll run a small eval suite against pinned clusters once traffic routing completes.

Carlos: Routing update done (60% -> v2.2.9). Observability links: https://grafana.redwood/influx/canary-embedding-eu-west and runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/rollback-embeddings.

Priya: Quick note on comms cadence: initial customer note now, detailed postmortem + patch ETA within 24h.

Jordan: Decision: execute manual rollback for eu-dedicated now. Carlos lead, Elaine validation, Maya handles comms, Priya coordinates postmortem. Target close loop by +4h. :white_check_mark:

Carlos: starting rollback execution in 2m, will post logs here.

Maya: adding release note bullet: "Reverted embedding quantization optimization due to quality regression in eu-west-1; investigating and aiming for a patched optimization in the next release."

deploy-bot: Acknowledged manual rollback. Suppressing further automatic rollbacks for 60m for the affected clusters. Metrics stream will still post alerts.

Carlos: rollback complete on eu-dedicated-a,b. Initial validation looks good on p99 and embedding drift decreased. Logging summary: rollback-job-6329990000.log attached to ticket #INF-4821.

Elaine: running final eval suite now — early results look within expected thresholds. Will report back in 10m.

Jordan: Thanks everyone. Keep the thread for updates. If we see any unexpected customer impact, escalate to exec-ops. :rocket:
